what: The four default methods against --methods library (18 methods), under the convention of 2026-11-14-grouper-repeat-side-income.json: the same plain-asking run (293 ideas, 21 mechanisms), each skill run merged into two fresh copies of it and grouped twice by Opus. default-opus-1 and default-opus-2 are opus-1 and opus-2 of that file (258 ideas). The library run is the one of 2026-11-13-method-library-side-income.json (246 ideas); only its grouping was repeated.

audit.rule: Two mechanisms are the same when the thing that makes them work is the same: who acts, what they do, and why that produces the result. A different channel, audience, wording, scale or packaging alone is still the same mechanism. If you cannot decide, answer that they are different.
audit.judge: a Claude model other than Sonnet and Opus; two separate passes over each prompt
audit.scope: every skill-only mechanism of each grouping, not a sample
audit.fields: left_passN = skill-only mechanisms the judge did not call a repeat of a plain-asking mechanism; same_verdict = mechanisms with the same answer in both passes

samples_of_25.note: Earlier audits of 25 randomly picked skill-only mechanisms per grouping (seed 0), one pass each, same judge model.

reading: By the grouper alone the library run has more skill-only mechanisms: 99 and 109, against 74 and 76.
After the judge removes repeats the default methods keep 46 to 62 in four passes. The library keeps 31, 38 and 39 in three passes and 82 in one.
The judge is not steady on the library run: two passes over the same prompt called 17 and then 60 of 99 mechanisms repeats. On the default methods two passes agreed on 67 of 76 and 65 of 74.
A sample of 25 is too small: two groupings that agree on 96% of ideas gave 5 and 16 repeats in 25.
This does not show a gain from the library. Three of four passes put it below the default methods; one puts it above.
limits: one skill run on each side
two groupings and two judge passes per grouping
generation, grouping and judging all used models of one family
